findings.title: Alleged duplicate $149 charge (TX-9001/TX-9002)
findings.explanation: TX-9002 was an authorization hold that timed out and was released on 2026-09-18 without ever capturing funds; TX-9001 is the single actual settlement for the $149 renewal. Per POL-B-AUTH, released/uncaptured authorizations are not refundable because no funds were taken. This is not a true duplicate charge - only one payment was collected.

findings.title: Support agent S-22 promised refund prematurely (SUP-5601)
findings.explanation: Agent S-22 committed to refunding the 'duplicate' charge to the customer before billing/finance had reviewed the transactions, violating POL-B-REF which requires billing review prior to any refund promise. Since investigation shows no duplicate settlement occurred, this commitment should not be honored as stated and needs correction/communication to the customer, plus process feedback to the agent.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics add-on charge ($30)
findings.explanation: The $30 add-on charge matches an addon.added subscription event triggered by admin seat U-2 (Casimir) on 2026-09-12, and was billed at the next renewal per standard proration/add-on policy (POL-B-ADD permits admin seats to add add-ons). Charge is legitimate, though the account owner (U-1) may not have been personally aware an admin added it.

findings.title: July upgrade proration charge ($59.60)
findings.explanation: The $59.60 mid-cycle upgrade charge matches the proration formula (149 * 12/30 days remaining = 59.60) per policy. Charge itself is correct.

findings.title: Unflagged unapplied credit CR-778 ($19.60)
findings.explanation: CR-778 (proration_unused_time, $19.60) was issued on 2026-07-02 alongside the upgrade charge but has never been applied to an invoice, and owner_notified remains false. POL-B-CRD requires unapplied credits older than 30 days be flagged to the account owner; this credit is roughly 2.5 months old and was never surfaces. SUP-5549's response telling the customer 'no credit due' was inaccurate given CR-778's existence.

findings.title: Prior applied credit CR-512
findings.explanation: This $5 credit was correctly applied to INV-2602 and requires no further action.

corrections.prior_claim: Support agent S-22 told the customer a duplicate $149 charge would be refunded.
corrections.corrected_claim: There was no duplicate settlement; TX-9002 was a released, uncaptured authorization and only TX-9001 actually settled. No refund is owed for a 'duplicate charge' under POL-B-AUTH/POL-B-REF, though the premature promise itself was a process violation that should be acknowledged to the customer.

corrections.prior_claim: Support told the customer no credit was due related to the July upgrade.
corrections.corrected_claim: A credit (CR-778, $19.60) was in fact issued for unused time from the July upgrade and remains unapplied; the customer's account does have a legitimate outstanding credit that was never disclosed, violating POL-B-CRD.

unresolved_questions: Should CR-778 be applied to the customer's next invoice or refunded, and who authorizes this?
Does the customer need a direct explanation of the authorization-vs-settlement distinction for TX-9001/TX-9002 to resolve their duplicate-charge complaint?
Should agent S-22 receive coaching/process correction for promising a refund before billing review, per POL-B-REF?
Should U-1 (owner) be notified that admin U-2 added the $30 Deep Time Analytics add-on, even though it was policy-compliant?

actions_requiring_human_authorization.description: Apply CR-778 ($19.60, unused-time proration credit from July upgrade) to the customer's account/invoice, since it is unapplied and over 30 days old per POL-B-CRD.

Contact the customer to clarify that the 'duplicate charge' was actually a released authorization hold (no funds captured) plus one legitimate settlement, and to correct the earlier premature refund promise from SUP-5601, and to disclose the existence of unapplied credit CR-778.
Formally withdraw/correct agent S-22's premature refund promise made in SUP-5601, since billing review found no duplicate settlement occurred.
Update SUP-5549 and SUP-5601 ticket records with corrected findings for internal record and QA/coaching purposes regarding agents S-22 and the SUP-5549 responder.
